fact: ST DIGITAL, a pan-African data centre operator, says it has infrastructure deployed in Congo (among seven countries) hosting clients such as banks, telecom operators, public administrations and enterprises; no Congo facility is named.

ST DIGITAL states, as operator, that its data centres across its seven countries including Congo are Tier 3 / TIA-942 constructed facilities; the document names no Congo facility and does not separate Congo from the others (document published date used as as_of).

Xalam Analytics estimates about 3 live commercial (third-party colocation) data centre facilities in Congo in 2025, with about 1 MW live critical IT load, about 60% occupied by third-party customers, and all commercial capacity controlled by telecoms providers; the facilities are not named.

ARPCE, the regulator, put its Pointe-Noire data centre (156 m2, 54 racks) into service on 28 February 2024; ARPCE's director general says it can host the data of public administration and of the private sector.
ARPCE describes its Pointe-Noire data centre, in service since 28 February 2024, as Tier 3+ (operator's own statement, no certification named).

The document describes the Pointe-Noire Tier 3+ data centre as the ARPCE's own, the Agency for the Regulation of Posts and Electronic Communications, a state regulator, put into service on 2024-02-28.

The ministry reports that on 28 February 2024 the President commissioned in Pointe-Noire the ARPCE data centre (54 racks), connected to the WACS and 2Africa cables and able to host the data of public administration and of the private sector.
The ministry describes the ARPCE Pointe-Noire data centre, put into service 28 February 2024, as Tier 3+ (operator/ministry statement, no Uptime or TIA-942 certification cited).
